preliminary_cost.interpretation: Fresh pilot-40 recovered much of the generic nine-pair penalty but did not beat a favorable precommitted split in this small synthetic family. Later freeze discarded more useful pilot evidence and was slower.

nested_alpha_family_correction.correction: The earlier pi=1/9 pairwise union insurance is valid but not tight because all reporting intervals for one channel are nested in alpha. For arbitrary same-history selection, fixed per-channel caps beta_1+beta_2<=.05 dominate the selected miscoverage events and remove K from the bound.
nested_alpha_family_correction.original_grid: max alpha in each channel is .045. A symmetric coordinate envelope therefore scales all grid alphas by 5/9 so the maxima become .025/.025, adding log(1.8)=.5878 nats rather than log 9=2.1972.
nested_alpha_family_correction.power_boundary: For monotone interval-width/stopping utility the cap pair itself dominates every candidate lying below those caps. In the preliminary V3 family the scaled grid and fixed .025/.025 stopped on exactly the same eight paths/times. Thus K-free envelope validity does not itself create useful adaptive allocation; meaningful adaptation still needs selection-specific structure or fresh confirmation.
nested_alpha_family_correction.near_tightness: Independent e-values with cap-level spikes yield 1-.975^2=.049375 selected miscoverage under an adversarial selector, close to the .05 symmetric envelope limit.

target_decision_vs_numeric_reporting.result: Even a bottleneck-balancing selector that gives more alpha to the weaker channel at the fixed safety target can have 8.7975% selected numerical-CI miscoverage in an exact e-value-family counterexample away from the target. Fixed-null decision routing and unknown-true-parameter numerical coverage are distinct statistical problems.
target_decision_vs_numeric_reporting.implication: Do not use apparent safety of decision-IUT target evidence as a proof for same-history numerical reporting-alpha selection.

closed_test_status.result: Weighted-average e-value closure can improve fixed finite-hypothesis FWER, but for unrestricted numeric marginal CIs, closure requires protecting intersections against every nuisance value. When the other channel e-value can attain infimum 0, projection gives the same weighted-Bonferroni threshold. No free V3 marginal-report gain has been established from closure.

measurement_validity_rules: Exploit nested alpha families before generic multiplicity accounting; per-pair union insurance can be grossly conservative.
A validity envelope that allows arbitrary selection may be statistically dominated by its single cap pair; report adaptive power, not merely the existence of multiple valid selectable pairs.

Decision-IUT and numerical reporting have opposite error geometries: full alpha per component can be valid for an intersection-union decision while simultaneous numerical bounds require union-of-miscoverage control.
For meaningful adaptive numerical reporting without same-history model assumptions, freeze the selector on a pilot prefix and use fresh conditionally-valid confirmation.
scope_guards: All numeric stop-time comparisons here are small synthetic stresses except the exact algebraic/counterexample probabilities.
Nested-envelope correction does not prove impossibility of a more powerful selector-specific same-history method.
Target-selector counterexample is abstract and does not claim deployed V3 failure.
